t:
A body B is capable of remaining stationary inside a liquid at the position shown in Fig. (a). If the whole system is gently placed on smooth inclined plane (Fig (b)) and is allowed to slide down, then (0<θ<90°). The body will
[[img:6c81c2522c4a]]
s:
Initially, the body is stationary inside the liquid. This means the buoyant force perfectly balances the weight of the body.
Let the density of the body be ρ and the density of the liquid be σ. Let V be the volume of the body. For equilibrium, the weight equals the buoyant force: Vρg=Vσg, which gives ρ=σ.
When the system is placed on a smooth inclined plane of angle θ, it accelerates downwards along the incline. The acceleration of the entire system (container and liquid) is a=gsinθ.
We analyze the forces on the body in the non-inertial reference frame of the accelerating container. In this frame, we must consider the effective acceleration due to gravity, defined as g⃗_(eff)=g⃗−a⃗.
We resolve g⃗ and a⃗ into components parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane:
Component of g⃗_(eff) parallel to the incline is gsinθ−a=gsinθ−gsinθ=0.
Component of g⃗_(eff) perpendicular to the incline is gcosθ.
Thus, g⃗_(eff) has a magnitude of gcosθ and points perpendicularly into the inclined plane.
In this accelerating frame, the forces acting on the body are its effective weight and the buoyant force, both of which are determined by g⃗_(eff).
Effective weight of the body: W⃗_(eff)=mg⃗_(eff)=Vρg⃗_(eff)
Buoyant force: F⃗_B=−m_(liquid)g⃗_(eff)=−Vσg⃗_(eff)
The net force on the body relative to the liquid is the sum of these two forces:
F⃗ₙₑₜ=W⃗_(eff)+F⃗_B=Vρg⃗_(eff)−Vσg⃗_(eff)=V(ρ−σ)g⃗_(eff)
Since we established initially that ρ=σ, it follows that F⃗ₙₑₜ=0.
Because the net force on the body in the frame of the liquid is zero, the body will remain stationary relative to the liquid.
o: move up for some inclination θ and will move down for another inclination θ

t: A horizontal tube has different cross sections at points A and B. The area of cross section are a₁ and a₂, respectively, and pressures at these points are p₁=ρgh₁ and p₂=ρgh₂, where ρ is the density of liquid flowing in the tube and h₁ and h₂ are heights of liquid columns in vertical tubes connected at A and B. If h₁−h₂=h, then the flow rate of the liquid in the horizontal tube is
s:
Let a₁ and a₂ be cross sectional areas and v₁ and v₂ the velocities of liquid flow at A and B. If p₁ and p₂ are pressures of liquid recorded by manometer, then p₁+1/2pv₁²=p₂+1/2ρv₂²
⇒p₁−p₂=1/2ρv₁²(v₂²/v₁²−1)
By equation of continuity, a₁v₁=a₂v₂
Also, p₁−p₂=hpg
Substituting these values, we have v₁=√(2gh/(a₁²/a₂²−1))
Rate of flow of liquid is a₁v₁=a₁a₂√(2gh/(a₁²−a₂²)) !

s:
Velocity of efflux from the orifice is given by Torricelli’s law v=√2gh.
The rate of mass flow of water leaving the tank is dm/dt=ρav.
The thrust force exerted on the tank due to the ejected water is F=vdm/dt=ρav².
Substituting v²=2gh, the force becomes F=2ρagh.
Given values are ρ=1000 kg/m³, a=5×10⁻⁴ m², h=2 m, and g=10 m/s².
Substituting the values into the force equation:
F=2×1000×5×10⁻⁴×10×2=20 N.
The initial horizontal acceleration of the tank is a′=F/M, where M is the total mass.
a′=20/50=0.4 m/s².

t: What is the absolute pressure (in atm) on a swimmer 10 m below the surface of a lake? Take atmospheric pressure 1×10⁵ N/m²
s: The formula used to calculate the absolute pressure, the pressure that varies with the depth of the fluid is given as follows: P=P₀+ρgh We need to substitute the given parameters in the above equation as, P_S=P_A+ρgh In the question we are provided that the pressure exerted by the air is equal to 1.01×10⁵ Pa, the depth at which the swimmer is swimming is 10 m and the density of the vater is 1000 kg/m³. Upon substituting the above values in the above equation, we get, P_S=1.01×10⁵+1000×10×10 On calculating these values we get, P_S=2×10⁵ Pa Now we need to perform the unit conversion, that is, the value of the pressure we have obtained is in terms of the Pascal, but in the options, the unit used is atm, so we will convert the unit to the same. The conversion factor from Pascal to atmosphere is, 1 Pa=10⁻⁵ atm Using this relation, we will convert the unit of the pressure value obtained. So, we get, P_S=(2×10⁵)×10⁻⁵ So on doing the calculation we have, P_S=2 atm Hence the pressure on the swimmer is 2 atm.
